I wonder what would happen if the target managed to evade the arms until dawn. (I realize it would have to be some extraordinarily lucky target with an entire army protecting them, but hypotheticals are fun.) Would they go away? If so, would they then come back the next night…?

And the usual question I have about any skip that hunts you down and won't stop until you're dead: what about immortals? Whether respawning like Able, body-hopping like Bright, or just unkillable to begin with, what would the arms do if it just couldn't destroy its target completely?

item.content:encoded:
Dr. Alto Clef strode confidently through the hallways of Site-23, boldly pushing those in his way aside to make a clear path for the mob of junior assistants behind him. He found locker 51164 and laughed heartily. Clef turned around to face the crowd.

"Today," he exclaimed heartily. "You shall witness the defiance of death!"

The crowd whooped and cheered as the good doctor opened the locket and activated the object.

"Watch! Friends, co-workers, watch! See how no response comes forth? See the power of the great, the mighty—"

Alto froze. His speech was cut off with a whrrr. He slowly turned back towards the object, noticing the piece of paper emerging from the machine. He tentatively picked it up.

SOMEONE'S a rude-ass motherfucker tumut

Clef died the next day at 1:43.

POINT IS. Clef is not that character you seem to make him out to be. Hell, there was an entire contest full of entries where the prompt was "The Death of Alto Clef." :|

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Your question hinges on the assumption that the Foundation's claim D class are all criminals is true. That's not exactly a safe assumption to make. Many users feel that the Ds are actually recruited off the street, and that the death row backstory is a fabrication to keep researchers from trying to rescue them.

That said, note that there are no good fortunes. I prefer the interpretation that the fortune telling booth dispenses a fortune because it's a fortune telling booth and they do that, but all the fortunes are bad and generally psychological shots in the dark because it's not a nice object at all.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Maybe, maybe not.

The problem with some of the Foundation's testing methods is that, from an outside perspective, both the test subjects and the testers are mostly "morally gray" - something that judges based on moral character may well judge them all to be on the same level. In fact, considering SOME of the things written here, the scientists are often FAR worse then the D-Class they deal with.

Somewhere there's a test log about some SCP that uses the test subject's morality, and it turns out the subject was innocent (or sorta). The log notes the fact, that he was terminated, and asks for more innocent test subjects to confirm the hypothesis.

A researcher fed TWO children to SCP-682 before Clef fed him to it, implying that they have (or can get) any test subjects they want for destructive testing. (That's what we at the Foundation call "Tuesday"!)

There are a lot of awful people there. As for the nice ones, they still work side by side with the psychos.

Welcome to the Foundation!
